title: EU Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix and Residency Enforcement
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a tenant-scoped authorization matrix and enforcement layer that guarantees EU-only data residency and routing for customers that opt into or require EU restrictions. This ticket defines the policy precedence, tenant configuration schema, routing decision flow, runtime enforcement hooks, audit logging, and rollout strategy. The goal is to provide deterministic, auditable routing decisions (region + tier + model variant) that satisfy legal/regulatory EU residency constraints and customer allowlist/denylist controls.
spec:
Overview:
We will add a Tenant Routing Authorization Matrix (TRAM) that is evaluated at request ingress and used by the Smart Routing engine. TRAM is tenant-scoped (applies to org or project depending on tenant_id) and supports multiple policy axes: residency_constraints (enum: eu_only, any_region, region_allowlist), allowed_tiers (list: hosted,dedicated,private), model_variant_preference (map: role->preferred_variant), and explicit_customer_allow/deny lists for special routing exceptions. Policy precedence: explicit denylist > tenant residency enforcement > per-route overrides (if permitted) > global defaults.

Routing decision flow (high level):
1) Ingress: request arrives with tenant_id and metadata (consent_header, jurisdiction_hint, route_id).
2) Resolve tenant TRAM config from tenant-config cache (fast-path). If missing, call Tenant Policy Service with cache miss metric.
3) Evaluate compliance predicates: does request require EU residency? Is tenant in EU-only mode? Is the requested route marked as cross-border-allowed?
4) Candidate pool selection: choose model variants and deployment regions matching allowed_tiers and residency constraints. If no candidate satisfies strict residency, move to fallback policy (see fallback section).
5) Authorization check: consult tenant-level allowlist/denylist for special customer exceptions (IP/routing tags).
6) Finalize decision, annotate request trace, and forward to Serving Runtime via routing API.

Fallback policy:
- Strict mode (tenant residency_constraints == eu_only AND fail_on_violation==true): reject request with 403 and audit log.
- Soft mode (default): fallback to EU-compatible model variant in hosted or dedicated EU pool. If none available, route to degraded model with redaction tag and notify customer via header X-Redwood-Routing-Fallback. Telemetry increments fallback_used.

Policy update semantics:
- TRAM updates are versioned. Each change creates a policy_version id.
api_changes:
New endpoints and headers:
- GET /v1/tenant/{tenant_id}/tram -> returns current TRAM config and policy_version.
- POST /internal/routing/decide -> internal API used by edge to request decision; payload: {tenant_id, route_id, jurisdiction_hint, consent_header, preferred_zone}. Response: {decision_id, region, tier, model_variant, policy_version, reason}.
- New response headers for routed requests: X-Redwood-Routing-Decision, X-Redwood-Policy-Version, X-Redwood-Routing-Fallback (when applicable).
Auth: internal endpoints require mTLS and service-to-service JWT with scope: routing:decide.
Backwards compatibility: default when tenant has no TRAM is legacy routing behavior; feature flag 'tram-enforce' will gate enforcement during rollout.
data_model_changes:
Tenant config storage (KV store + DB index):
- New table/collection 'tenant_tram' with columns (tenant_id, residency_constraints, allowed_tiers, model_variant_map, allowlist, denylist, fail_on_violation, policy_version, updated_by, updated_at).
- Cache key: tram:{tenant_id}:{policy_version}.
- Audit logs: each routing decision writes a compact audit record to routing_audit (decision_id, tenant_id, timestamp, decision, reason, policy_version, route_id, request_id).
Note: Use existing config migration tooling; add DB migration script and store initial policy_version = 1 when creating TRAM entries.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 - Canaries (2 weeks):
- Enable read-only TRAM on edge to record decisions and diffs; do not enforce. Collect mismatch_count metric.
- Target 5% of tenants (low-risk) + 100% of EU-region traffic for visibility.

Phase 2 - Soft enforcement (2 weeks):
- Enable soft mode for 20% tenants. Fallback to EU-compatible variants and emit headers. Add customer notifications for impacted tenants.

Phase 3 - Strict enforcement (gradual):
- Opt-in tenants can flip to strict mode. After 1 month of low mismatch, enable strict mode for customers who have completed verification.

Phase 4 - Full enforcement:
- Enable a tenant onboarding flow in Console and APIs. Announce breaking change 30 days prior.

Rollback: Feature flag tram-enforce can be disabled globally to temporarily stop enforcement and revert to legacy routing.

Operational readiness: runbook added to SRE playbook: 'tram-routing-failure' with steps to identify cache, policy_version mismatch, and circuit-break to legacy routing.
testing_plan:
Unit tests: policy evaluation, precedence rules, and schema validation.
Integration tests: end-to-end decision path with mocked Tenant Policy Service, including cache miss, allowlist/denylist checks, and fallback behaviors.
E2E canary tests: route sample traffic for tenants with various TRAM configs and assert routing decisions satisfy residency constraints.
Security tests: penetration review for internal endpoints, ensure audit logs are tamper-evident.
Performance tests: latency benchmark on routing/decide endpoint under 5k rps; ensure added median latency < 2ms.
QA checklist: verify header emission, audit log format, policy_version increments, and 403 response format for strict mode.
NOTE: Add test vectors for cross-border-consent header set/unset, and for tenant-level denylist entries (IP and route tags).
acceptance_criteria: Edge can fetch TRAM for tenant and make routing decisions with <=2ms added latency on 95th percentile
Fallback_used telemetry increments and is visible in Console metrics when fallback occurs
Policy precedence enforced: denylist entries block specified routes regardless of other settings
Audit records for 100% of decisions are written to routing_audit and available for query
Canary mismatch rate < 0.05% before enabling strict mode for that cohort
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Ticket created; initial spec drafted. Assigned to Marco Rivera.
2026-03-11 - Sync with Policy Service team; agreed on versioned TRAM schema and cache key format.
2026-03-12 - PoC for internal routing/decide endpoint implemented; basic residency predicate passes local tests.
Next - implement DB migration and add audit log writer; coordinate with Console team for header display and tenant UI.
notes: Design trade-offs: storing full allowlist in cache increases memory but reduces policy-eval latency; we opted for an LRU sharded cache with tombstones for denies.
Consider exposing a dry-run mode in Console so customers can preview how their traffic would be routed under TRAM rules.
Need legal review for EU residency definitions (e.g., handling of non-EU data processors in EU-region deployments).
